2607.28959.title: Efficient LLM Adversarial Training via Low-Rank Defense and Circuit-Guided Surrogates
2607.28959.paper_summary: Adversarial training is one of the most effective defenses against adversarial attacks, yet the computational cost remains prohibitive at modern scales, especially for large language models (LLMs). While existing mitigation strategies, e.g., latent adversarial training (LAT), have been developed, they still incur a high computational cost. In this work, we comprehensively investigate computation-efficient strategies to speed up LAT from two complementary perspectives: (1) Defense-side optimization: We explore the representation fine-tuning (ReFT) within LAT, and reveal a potential issue if there is a mismatch on which tokens to apply ReFT and the attack. (2) Attack-side optimization: When computing adversarial attacks in each LAT iteration, we extract only the relevant circuits from the LLM to construct a lightweight surrogate model, avoiding the computation in the forward-backward passes through the full model during the attack generation. For both perspectives, we provide theoretical justifications and numerical evidence to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed strategies. Ultimately, compared to standard LAT with full fine-tuning, our method on average reduces per-step adversarial-training FLOPs by 48.1% while requiring only 0.0118% trainable parameters.
2607.28959.paper_summary_zh: 對抗訓練是對抗攻擊中最有效的防禦之一，但在現代規模下，計算成本仍然過高，特別是對於大型語言模型（LLMs）。雖然已有現有的緩解策略，例如潛在對抗訓練（LAT），但它們仍然需要高昂的計算成本。在這項工作中，我們從兩個互補的角度全面研究計算高效的策略以加速LAT：（1）防禦端優化：我們探討了LAT中的表示微調（ReFT），並揭示了如果在應用ReFT的標記和攻擊之間存在不匹配，可能會出現的潛在問題。（2）攻擊端優化：在每次LAT迭代中計算對抗攻擊時，我們僅提取LLM中的相關電路來構建輕量級的替代模型，避免在攻擊生成過程中對整個模型進行前向和反向傳遞的計算。對於這兩個角度，我們提供了理論依據和數值證據，以說明所提出策略的有效性。最終，與全微調的標準LAT相比，我們的方法平均減少每步對抗訓練的FLOPs 48.1%，同時僅需0.0118%的可訓練參數。
